notes: *let … be* is taken as the jussive form of the construction-supplied copula on the prepositional predicate כְּ, headed on *as* (rules 49, 20); giving *let* to the substantival participle instead was the competing reading.

*when he goeth forth* stays with the infinitive צֵאת because the כְּ has already spent its own English word on *as*, and a preposition holding a word of its own is not a home for a second (rule 52's count).
תִּשְׁקֹט → *had rest* headed on the complement (rule 44); the vocative יְהוָה takes the supplied *O* (rule 36).
